thread:
Alex W: Quick sync — I'm floating an "on-demand baseline + spot burst" policy for eu-west to cut unit costs. Proposal: keep a small guaranteed on-demand baseline per AZ for latency-sensitive inference, allow automatic spot bursting up to X% of fleet, and soft-fallback to other regions or cheaper instance families if spots drop. Looking for concerns on SLO, networking, and interruption ops.
Marta P: How are you calculating the baseline size? p95 latency for online low-latency workloads is 200ms, and cold-starts kill that.
Alex W: Baseline = max(steady_concurrency / instances_per_gpu, min_capacity), where steady_concurrency is a 95th of recent qps per model. Rough rule: baseline = ~20-25% of total needed to handle steady traffic without batching. We keep it per-AZ to avoid cross-AZ latencies.
Liam S: +1 for per-AZ. Also add a small warm pool (hot cache) on each baseline node so we don't have model load time. If spot bursts land, they should attach to the same local KV cache placement.
Jordan (oncall): Cross-AZ fallback has egress + latency hit. If we fallback to another region we need explicit opt-in per-customer. Also note regulatory customers can't cross region.
Marta P: Right — so fallback policy must be configurable per-customer and per-model. Can we make burst-to-spot allowed only for non-PHI customers?
Alex W: Yep. Policy model: allowlist per-customer, default deny for regulated tags. Implementation sketch: per-deployment tunables: `min_on_demand`, `burst_ratio`, `allow_cross_az`, `allow_cross_region`. Example config shown below.
```
{
  "min_on_demand": 6,                // per-AZ baseline gpus
  "burst_ratio": 3.5,               // max multiple of baseline that can be spot
  "max_spot_percent": 75,           // cap overall spot percentage
  "fallback": "prefer_local_on_demand, then az_spot, then region_spot",
  "preempt_budget": 0.05            // fraction of running work to allow preempt at a time
}
```
Liam S: For interruption handling: don't cancel in-flight requests. Evict spot instances into 'draining' state and let runtime migrate KV cache if possible. We need a fast kv-sync to avoid cold penalty.
Jordan (oncall): Also track `preempt_count` and set alerts when it spikes. Preempt spikes can correlate with noisy neighbors or cloud maintenance windows.
Alex W: Cost math: in eu-west baseline-only run = $X/hr. With 70% spot we estimate ~45-55% cost reduction depending on spot volatility. We should simulate tail-preemption cost (e.g., retry extra tokens) in our estimator.
Marta P: How about hedging across instance families? If p3X is scarce, let bursts try a cheaper GPU family with lower perf but still acceptable for batch/rerank jobs.
Liam S: Hedging is good. We'll need model/QoS profiles — e.g., strict models pinned to T4/foe, flexible ones allowed on A100-variants or mixed quantized instances.
Alex W: Operational playbook notes:
- If preemptions > threshold for > 5m, throttle new spot allocations and raise on-call.
- If cross-az egress > budget, reduce cross-az fallback and favor local on-demand.
- Auto-rollout: start with burst_ratio=1.5 for 24h, ramp to 3.5 if preemptions low.
Jordan (oncall): Add a circuit-breaker metric `spot_health_score` (0-1) combining preempt_rate, reclaim_rate, and startup_latency. When <0.6, reduce spot usage automatically.
Alex W: Good call. I'll draft a PR that plumbs `spot_health_score` into the autoscaler and adds per-customer allowlists.
Marta P: Also can we add a cost-visibility dashboard per-deployment showing estimated savings vs added retry latency? Product will want that.
Liam S: I'll add metrics: `estimated_spot_savings`, `avg_retry_latency`, and `kv_warm_ratio`.
Alex W: Thanks — I'll open the RFC and tag y'all. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment config `onbaseline-spotburst-flag` created by Alex W for rollout testing.
Jordan (oncall): Minor nit — capture network egress estimate in the estimator (GB * $/GB) when region fallback enabled. We had a surprise last month.
Alex W: noted. Will include egress cost and a hard cap per-customer.
Marta P: Cool. If the RFC covers these points I'm happy to approve the pilot.
Liam S: Happy to help on implementation.
Alex W: Great — thanks everyone.
